headline: Ranked Rivals Clash in Eastern Atlantic Opener
subhead: Two 0-1 top-ten teams meet with conference positioning at stake.

xFactor.why: NicU Iamaleava ranks fifth in the PCFL with 282 passing yards and three touchdowns.

keyMatchup: Alabama's fifth-ranked passing attack against a Boston College defense allowing 468 yards per game.
body: Alabama brings the PCFL's fifth-ranked passer in NicU Iamaleava, who threw for 282 yards and three scores in the opener, and the league's second-leading receiver in Terrill Fields with 139 yards and a touchdown. The Crimson Tide offense averages 348 yards per game, 13th in the league, paced by 290 yards through the air against just 58 on the ground. Boston College counters with a defense yielding 468 yards per game, 14th in the PCFL, while its own offense managed 242 total yards, 16th overall, split between 147 passing and 95 rushing.

Both teams sit 0-1 and fourth and third respectively in the Eastern Atlantic, each allowing at least 29 points per game. Alabama's defense gave up 599 yards in Week 1, the league's worst mark, while Boston College's unit allowed 468. Marv Quirk recorded an interception for Alabama, tying for third in the PCFL, offering a potential turnover spark. The matchup pits the Tide's aerial strength against an Eagles defense that has yet to prove it can contain a high-volume passing game.
